source_ref: Guo W, Wang J, Li N, Wang L (2025) The impact of teacher emotional support on learning engagement among college students mediated by academic self-efficacy and academic resilience. Sci Rep 15:3670, doi:10.1038/s41598-025-88187-x, PMC11779917 (CC BY 4.0). Supplementary Table S1 41598_2025_88187_MOESM1_ESM.xlsx (the article's only supplementary file; fetched from static-content.springer.com 2026-09-29, sha256 4a38a66386b7fc9406507771e488a3d704106f52c8073fcab20622ac7e998582, byte-identical to the copy used for guo_2025_ar in batch_733), sheet 1, header row 3, columns 20-41 (legend items 16-37); anchors from the row-2 legend. Processing script data/guo_2025_teacher_support.py.
note: ITEM TEXT: the 22 ASE column headers of the supplement, verbatim except the leading item number ('1.'..'22.') stripped; no leading/trailing whitespace in any header; source punctuation kept (item 22 uses a curly apostrophe). MAPPING: the header text sits on the column itself (data_labels), but the IRW code is assigned POSITIONALLY by the processing script (walks the 47 item columns in legend order tes15/ase22/ar5/le5 and asserts each header starts with 'k.'), so Step 5b re-ran that derivation: each live ase_k vector equals xlsx column 19+k for 414/414 respondents matched on id=Number; largest off-diagonal agreement 0.483 (verify_guo_2025_ase.R). ANCHORS: legend reads 'Response Scale: All items use a 5-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree)'; shipped those endpoint labels on all 22 items, resp 2-4 left blank (never labelled). The article words the endpoints 'completely disagree'/'completely agree'; the deposit legend was preferred as the level-1 source. No instructions published; left blank. INSTRUMENT: per the article, Liang Yusong's (2000, CCNU thesis) Chinese Academic Self-Efficacy Scale adapted from Pintrich & De Groot (1990), 22 items, two dimensions (learning behaviour / learning ability); the article does not publish the item-to-dimension key, so no section split. NEGATIVELY WORDED ITEMS 14, 16, 17, 20 (data caveat, not a text change): they correlate +0.30..+0.58 with positively worded items (e.g. ase_14 vs ase_13 +0.58) and have corrected item-total r 0.60-0.68, as high as any positive item; the article's ASE mean 3.618 / SD 0.766 / alpha 0.940 reproduce exactly with all 22 items as stored (3.618/0.766/0.940) and not with those four reversed (3.473/0.518/0.81). So the published scoring treats them as stored, but whether the stored values are raw agreement with the English negative wording or were already reversed cannot be settled from the deposit; the legend's single anchor statement was shipped unchanged and the ambiguity disclosed in public_note. LANGUAGE: administered in Chinese (Wenjuanxing survey, two Shandong universities; Liang's scale is a Chinese instrument). Checked the supplement xlsx (zero CJK in sharedStrings.xml and sheet1.xml; CJK only in styles/theme font names and docProps author) and the full PMC article XML (zero CJK): the Chinese wording is not recoverable from deposit or supplements, so the English header wording (the authors' own rendering) ships in the base fields as translated_substitute, language=Chinese, _translated columns empty. RIGHTS: two instruments in play. (a) Originator of the construct/source items: Pintrich & De Groot (1990) MSLQ self-efficacy items -- instrument_rights_register row 'MSLQ' verdict ship (public domain; 'citation only, no permission needed'), applied not re-derived. (b) The Chinese adaptation actually administered: Liang Y. (2000), master's thesis, Central China Normal University; no rights statement, fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause locatable (no publisher page exists for an unpublished thesis). The shipped English is the study's own rendering in a CC BY 4.0 supplement. Ships on silence; no register row written (rounds may not write ship rows) -- escalation candidate if Ben wants a Liang 2000 row.
public_note: Respondents read a Chinese version of these items; the wording shown is the study authors' own English rendering from their data deposit, as the Chinese wording was not published. The four negatively worded items (ase_14, ase_16, ase_17, ase_20) correlate positively (pairwise +0.25 to +0.59) with the positively worded items and the paper's reported scale mean reproduces only with them as stored, so it is unclear whether their stored values are raw agreement or already reverse-scored.

source_ref: Ha, Quiroz & McNeish (2026) Computers in Human Behavior 181:108981, doi 10.1016/j.chb.2026.108981, NIH author manuscript PMC13267910 (PMC OAI record fetched 2026-09-29, sha256 prefix 7456bd5279afd2f6), Methods > Measures > 'Daily affect'; deposit OSF 5b798 (CC BY 4.0) Data/ASPIRE Sexting Paper_Data_4.24.25 (with labels).csv column headers
note: Item codes are the deposit's own column headers minus the _A/_B partner suffix (data/ha_2026_aspire.py; code IS source name). The deposit has no codebook, no variable/value labels and no wording (header row only; the 'with labels' file just adds the header row; Mplus .inp/.out files name variables only). Words for 5 of 7 items come from the paper's Measures section, verbatim: 'participants indicated their positive and negative affect by rating five different items, including happy, energetic, low, irritable, and distressed' ... 'Items were rated on a Likert scale from 1 = Not at all to 7 = Very much.' happy->happy, energ->energetic, low->low, irr->irritable, distr->distressed: the codes are self-describing abbreviations of those adjectives. item_text is the bare adjective, matching the source's terseness; the paper prints no question stem or instructions, so instructions is blank. Anchors: resp 1 'Not at all', resp 7 'Very much'; 2-6 unlabelled and left blank. insec and attr: in the deposit (same 1-7 block, interleaved with the five) but NOT named anywhere in the paper; item_text AND option_text left blank rather than guessed (codes suggest 'insecure' and something like 'attracted'/'attractive'; polarity is consistent -- insec correlates +0.43..+0.56 with the negative items, attr +0.54..+0.55 with happy/energ -- but that does not establish wording). Paper's anchor sentence is scoped to the five items it lists, so it was not extended to insec/attr. Paper-vs-data count: the paper says 'five different items'; the deposit/IRW table has seven. Sample: paper analysed 98 mixed-gender couples; deposit has 101 couples (processing script's scope, not an item-text question). Sibling/earlier ASPIRE papers that might list all seven (Rogers et al. 2018 JYA 10.1007/s10964-017-0797-y closed; Ha et al. 2024 Dev Sci 10.1111/desc.13511 Wiley pdfdirect bot-walled, not in PMC) were not reachable. Rights: the wording is the study's own diary adjectives 'based on' the PANAS (Watson et al. 1988) and prior diary studies; instrument_rights_register.csv has PANAS=ship; no clause reserving any right located for these items. The PMC article license reads 'available for text mining ... fair use' (article-level notice, not a term on the items). Silence -> extract.
public_note: Item text is published for 5 of the 7 affect items (happy, energetic, low, irritable, distressed); insec and attr have no wording in the source paper or deposit, so their item_text and anchors are blank, and only the 1 (Not at all) and 7 (Very much) anchors of the 1-7 scale are labelled.
